rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection`. I did not request implementation source.

**Resolution from the root, returning an owned item**
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` selects every outline item by its selector. It asserts that `text()` equals the item's span in the source and that `structural_hash()` matches the item.
- It also selects the nested path `mod[auth]/fn[check]` and checks that attached docs and attributes are included in the text.
- The empty selector is covered in `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` (`selected.select("")` returns the root id and full text). `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` also checks the root selector.

**`id()` and `text()`**
- `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` asserts `id()` on both `from_id` and `select` results. It asserts `text()` on the selected content.
- The Markdown, CSS and Rust tests assert `text()` for selected items. The Rust test also checks the id, selector and span relationship for every item.

**Shared snapshot and fingerprinting rules**
- The Markdown and Rust tests assert `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())`. This shows the outline is shared.
- `explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme` checks that `selected.fingerprint_scheme()` is "custom-v2" after the language, clone and scheme are dropped. It checks that selections from loaded and supplied handles have equal fingerprints. It also checks that a different language configuration ("custom-v3") gives the same structural hash but a different fingerprint.
- The Rust test compares fingerprints across formatting-only and content changes.

**No additional read, and usable after the original handle is dropped**
- In `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits`, `file` is dropped and the file on disk is then rewritten.
- `selected_again`, which came from `file.select`, still returns "second". `selected.select("")` still returns the original full text. Meanwhile `from_id` fails on the edited file. This shows selection does not re-read the file.

**Selector rules followed**
- Percent-encoded names, `#N` duplicates and anonymous `kind@hash` segments are checked in `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items`. It selects `section[Same]#1` and `#2`, an anonymous `section@…`, a `block@…` and a re-selection from a selected item.
- `css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent` selects `#1`/`#2` items, including nested `media[print]#2/rule[a]`.
- Identical plain-text lines are covered in two tests. `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` checks that two identical `line` items both resolve. `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` and `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` select `line@hash` items.

**Errors for invalid, missing and ambiguous selectors**
- `missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors` checks a malformed selector (`fn[`) and a missing item (`fn[absent]`).
- `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` checks that duplicate `part[same]` items return an error containing "ambiguous". It also checks that duplicate `line[same]` items with different hashes return an ambiguity error.
- The CSS test asserts that `rule[a%20b]` without `#N` is an error.

**Residual points, not gaps**
- Only one malformed-selector form is tested.
- Selecting a nonexistent anonymous hash is not tested separately. It falls under the same "missing item" outcome as `fn[absent]`.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineId;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
File-read and parsing failures return errors, distinct from successful contents
for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that language's parsing
rules; a parse failure is reported rather than interpreted as plain text.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors` also returns an error.
